details: Bitcoin experienced a significant rally, climbing above $80,000 and reaching its highest level in over three months. This surge was primarily attributed to the U.S. Treasury's announcement of plans to double its buybacks of long-dated government bonds. This move led to a weakening of the U.S. dollar and a decline in bond yields, thereby increasing the attractiveness of non-yielding assets such as Bitcoin. The rally also triggered substantial liquidations of short positions in the cryptocurrency market, further amplifying the price increase and pushing market sentiment into "extreme greed" territory for the first time since late 2024.
title: Bitcoin Surges Past $80K on Treasury Buybacks, Dollar Weakness

details: The cryptocurrency market is anticipating increased volatility as several key U.S. economic indicators are slated for release this week. These include the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, which is the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, along with data on GDP growth and jobless claims. Remarks from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh at the upcoming Jackson Hole symposium are also highly awaited for further insights into the inflation and economic outlook. The outcome of these data releases will significantly influence the Federal Reserve's future monetary policy decisions, with stronger-than-expected data potentially dampening rate-cut expectations and negatively impacting risk assets, including cryptocurrencies. Conversely, weaker figures could bolster anticipation for easier monetary policy.
title: Crypto Market Braces for Volatility Ahead of US PCE, GDP, Jobs Data

details: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has announced "Operation Economic Outcast," a new global offensive aimed at disrupting Iran's financial networks. The initiative involves imposing sanctions on Iran's cryptocurrency, gold, shipping, aviation, and technology sectors. This comprehensive strategy is designed to close off all avenues for the Iranian regime to evade international sanctions and move money globally.
title: US Treasury Launches 'Operation Economic Outcast' Against Iran's Financial Networks

details: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is transitioning its monetary policy framework, moving from a system where the central bank directly controls reserves to one where commercial banks manage exchange settlement reserves. This shift is intended to gradually reduce the RBA's balance sheet through quantitative tightening and is expected to increase short-term funding volatility. This policy change holds relevance for the cryptocurrency sector as it touches upon critical areas such as Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) development, payments modernization, digital asset liquidity, and the broader adoption risks and opportunities for decentralized and centralized exchanges.
title: RBA Shifts Monetary Policy Framework, Affecting Digital Asset Liquidity
